records.subsection: Based on the model calculation, what amount of ISW depletion is recorded as a result of pumping specifically?
records.finding: Depletion volumes are produced by differencing a calibrated historical simulation against a counterfactual no-pumping simulation, yielding 504,400 AFY of in-Subbasin depletion plus 141,800 AFY of increased subsurface inflow, disaggregated by reach, neighbouring subbasin, month and water-year type.

The historical conditions simulation of the MercedWRM was used together with a newly developed simulation that removed pumping from the Merced Subbasin... records.section: 1.5 Per-well Attribution and the Cumulative Pumping Problem
records.subsection: How is the attribution of depletion carried out across space?
records.finding: 141,800 AFY of increased subsurface inflow from neighbouring subbasins is explicitly booked outside the Subbasin's own accounts. Interbasin MOUs exist but no mechanism reconciles the two sides of a shared boundary into a single depletion account.
records.direct_quote: "These impacts will eventually result in depletions, but because they occur outside of the Merced Subbasin they are accounted separately" — GSP §2.2.7, p. 2-195 [PDF 286]

records.subsection: Is there an accounting system for integration of these co-benefits?
records.finding: There is no combined accounting approach, common metric, stacking methodology or rule against double-counting a single physical outcome across categories — while the scoring explicitly rewards stacking.
records.direct_quote: Searched the MLRP RFP and Application — "Projects that address multiple Priority Criteria Categories will score higher than projects that address only one" (Application p. 10 [PDF 18]), and the rubric permits the same acreage to be claimed under DAC, Ecological and Geographic Prioritization simultaneously. The output is a point total, not quantities in different units.
records.notes: Merced's one working co-benefit mechanism achieves integrity by unbundling (ring-fencing habitat water), not by stacking — worth surfacing as a design tension.

records.subsection: What plans are there for mitigating dry wells?
records.finding: The Domestic Well Mitigation Program was adopted by all three GSA Boards in early 2026 and appears nowhere in the July 2026 Rules — no fee linkage, no trigger, no reporting obligation. Agricultural water accounting and domestic well protection run as parallel, unconnected systems.
records.direct_quote: Full-text search of the MSGSA Rules — the only place the Rules touch domestic wells is in defining what is exempt: de minimis extractors sit outside the consistency-determination monitoring requirements (§3.2.7). No reference to the Domestic Well Mitigation Program appears.
records.notes: The clearest structural expression in the Merced set of the two systems running unconnected. | Also touches 3.1.4 Domestic Well Protection.

records.finding: Merced acknowledges essentially no limitations regarding community engagement or equity accounting — in sharp contrast to the same documents' candour on technical matters, where failed data requests, a decommissioned CIMIS station, an unsuitable recharge site and shortfalls against contracted savings are all reported plainly.
records.direct_quote: Searched GSP §1.2.5, Periodic Evaluation §8 and the WY 2025 Annual Report — not acknowledged anywhere: that zero comments were received on the 2025 GSP; that DAC outreach is fully delegated with no verification or reach data; that the SAC has no decision authority; that no engagement metric is collected; that GSP-level materials are English-only; that no compensation is offered.
records.notes: The absence of any parallel reporting for community engagement more likely reflects that outcomes are not assessed than that all outcomes were good.

records.subsection: What specific value is pointed to for achieving sustainability?
records.finding: Turlock sets a quantitative, ISW-specific undesirable-result criterion that resolves at the river reach and is deliberately seasonally filtered to the Fall low-flow window — with the 50% threshold disclosed as an artifact of network sparsity and flagged for tightening.

records.notes: ISW is the most permissive trigger threshold in the GSP (50% vs 33% for other indicators), and the GSP says why.

records.direct_quote: Word-boundary searches for "interconnect*", "streamflow" and "stream depletion" across ETSGSA Rules Phase 1, Phase 2 and the Credit Calculation Policy return zero hits (positive controls: 164, 228 and 13 hits for "groundwater"). records.subsection: What specific value is pointed to for achieving sustainability?
records.finding: Two independent commenters — an NGO coalition and a federal fisheries agency — asked for a biological definition of the ISW undesirable result, and neither got one. The ecological question is externalised to the surface-water regulatory regime administered by the irrigation districts, which are themselves GSA member agencies.
records.direct_quote: Searched GSP §6.8 (ISW SMC) and the two places in Appendix F-15 Attachment C where a biological endpoint was requested (NGO Coalition, p. 8 of 19 [PDF 1260]; NMFS, p. 2 of 19 [PDF 1254]) — no biological or ecological criterion is adopted anywhere for the ISW indicator. Both responses point instead to existing GSP sections describing concerns and to instream flow requirements administered by the irrigation districts; a third routes to an ongoing Programmatic EIR.

records.subsection: How is water savings calculated?
records.finding: The siting method is quantitative and auditable — named thresholds (200 m stream buffer, 0.1 degree slope, 10 m DEM), named public datasets, an iterative overlay, and an aerial-imagery ground-truthing step.

records.notes: Rigour is concentrated at siting, not at verification — the cleanest single statement of the MLRP accounting problem in this project, and it is Turlock's own design.

records.subsection: How are those co-benefits tracked and quantified?
records.finding: An ecological monitoring instrument exists — a repeatable annual Vegetation/Habitat Quick Assessment on a fixed form — but cover is a four-bin ordinal, survival a visual estimate and habitat free-text notes, no threshold attaches to any value, and it is an optional per-project add-on even for Rewilding.
records.direct_quote: "Cover estimate for treated area (visual: <25%, 25–50%, 50–75%, >75%). Dominant species present (up to 5 common names ok); note target natives vs. invasives. records.subsection: Is dust considered in MLRP projects?
records.finding: In Turlock dust is a landowner liability, not a programme benefit — the inverse of the framing the co-benefit literature assumes. Every appearance frames dust as a nuisance to be avoided, and the one place it appears as a benefit is an explicitly optional best practice.
records.direct_quote: Word-boundary searches: dust appears 10 times across the Implementation Standards, 0 times in GSP Chapter 8, once in the Annual Report. Representative: "Maintain the land in a condition that does not create a nuisance because of, but not limited to, the following: fire danger, dust emissions, erosion..." (Implementation Standards, Rewilding, p. 2 [PDF 2]). "Decreased particulate and other air emissions" (Vegetated Cover, p. 1) is the only particulate reference in the entire MLRP corpus, with no measurement method.
records.notes: Confirms the two-basin dust gap in a stronger form than "no method exists": the agencies conceptualise the relationship in the opposite direction.

records.finding: The GSAs justify Chapter 3's incompleteness on the ground that outreach metrics change daily and should be published as close to GSP finalisation as possible — so the metrics are tracked in near-real time and oriented to the document rather than to programme management.
records.direct_quote: "several digital metrics depicting the depth of GSP outreach efforts (e.g. website visitors or YouTube video views) change daily, and it is prudent to update these metrics in Chapter 3 as close in time to finalizing the GSP as possible to provide the most up-to-date data describing public engagement efforts." — Attachment C, p. 5 of 19 [PDF 1257]
records.notes: Measured, published, and not used to change anything — the sharper version of "measured outreach, unmeasured effect."

records.subsection: What specific value is pointed to for achieving sustainability?
records.finding: HEADLINE. The 2020 GSP set a volumetric ISW minimum threshold (69,700 AF/yr, MO and all interim milestones identical). Amendment 1 replaced it entirely with a groundwater-elevation proxy at shallow wells. The stated reason is operational, not scientific: the model could not be run annually. This is the only instance in the three-basin study of a GSA adopting volumetric ISW accounting and then formally abandoning it.
records.direct_quote: "The 2020 GSP based depletion on a modeled quantity; however, it is unrealistic that the SVIHM will be updated annually to make this determination. GSP Amendment 1 aligns with the approach of the 2022 Salinas Valley GSPs that monitors depletion of ISW by proxy through shallow groundwater levels near locations of interconnection." (Periodic Evaluation 2.7.1, PDF p78)
records.notes: MOST GAP-RELEVANT SENTENCE IN THE SALINAS VALLEY SET. The binding constraint on volumetric ISW accounting was the cost/feasibility of running the model every year. records.subsection: What specific value is pointed to for achieving sustainability?
records.finding: Reservoir conservation releases are excluded from threshold applicability entirely, on the reasoning that depleting deliberately-released recharge water is the intended outcome. Defensible and clearly reasoned - but the Salinas River is reservoir-dominated in exactly the summer months when pumping peaks, and no document quantifies how much of the year or of the interconnected reach-length falls inside the carve-out.
records.direct_quote: "No minimum thresholds are established for times when flow in a river is due to conservation releases from a reservoir. One purpose for these conservation releases is to recharge the Salinas Valley Groundwater Basin. Therefore, depletion of conservation releases is a desired outcome, and the minimum thresholds and measurable objectives do not apply to these flows." (Amendment 1 8.11.2, PDF p325)
records.notes: Record as an UNQUANTIFIED exclusion, not an improper one. Genuinely transferable design question for GAP: how should an accounting platform treat managed recharge releases in an ISW ledger? Restated at Periodic Evaluation 2.7.3 (PDF p81).

records.subsection: Well permitting - stream proximity criterion
records.finding: No crediting, permitting, or mitigation mechanism of any kind is tied to ISW anywhere in the document set. No stream-proximity setback for new wells, no ISW-conditioned permit criterion, no mitigation requirement for pumping near interconnected reaches, no ISW credit, no ISW-specific reporting obligation on any extractor.

Well permitting is expressly another agency's function - Amendment 1 3.11.3, PDF p94: 'Monterey County is responsible for well permitting.' County ordinances 5302, 5303 and 5339 are directed at the Deep Aquifers, seawater intrusion, and a post-Protecting Our Water moratorium - none is keyed to stream proximity or ISW.
records.notes: THREE FOR THREE. records.subsection: Is the compliance loop (modeling and estimation outputs that translate into thresholds, then into policy, then into outcomes that feed policy) closed?
records.finding: Because the ISW MT is set numerically identical to the groundwater-level MT, the GSA reasons that ISW cannot have impacted groundwater levels. True as arithmetic and vacuous as accounting: an indicator defined as identical to another can never diverge from it, so it can never independently signal anything.
records.direct_quote: "Depletion of ISW is measured by proxy using groundwater elevations, and the SMC are set at the same levels as the groundwater level SMC. Therefore, depletion of ISW has not impacted groundwater levels." (Periodic Evaluation 2.7.4, PDF p81)
records.notes: The same construction recurs for every other indicator in 2.7.4. This is the precise mechanism guaranteeing the ISW indicator produces no information the groundwater-level indicator did not already produce. Structurally the same as Merced (ISW rides the level proxy passively) but stated more explicitly here.

records.subsection: What approach or combination of approaches is used to measure depletion of interconnected surface water? (field measurements & models)
records.finding: The most sophisticated ISW FIELD work in the three-basin corpus: five independent direct-measurement methods applied to a 6-mile reach, producing quantified sub-reach seepage rates and hydraulic conductivities. Nothing comparable exists in the Merced or East Turlock document sets.
records.direct_quote: "A variety of field methods were then implemented to evaluate river seepage rates within the Somavia Reach: a) high-precision synoptic-flow surveys to detail flow losses through the reach; b) streamflow gaging to assess seasonal sub-reach losses; c) shallow piezometer clusters to assess seasonal changes to vertical head gradients; d) riverbed temperature profiler time-series data to calibrate the USGS 1DTempPro model to estimate infiltration; and d) ring-infiltrometer measurements to estimate infiltration and hydraulic conductivity of riverbed, overbank and alternate channel alluvium." (ISW Report Executive Summary, PDF p7)
records.notes: Report's own list letters run a)-d) with 'd)' used twice; transcribed verbatim. Quantified results incl. 'On average, losses were 11 cfs/rm from Chualar to the Downstream Bend 1 gaging station, then lowering to 3.4 cfs/rm... and then to 1.0 cfs/rm from Bend 2 to Spreckels' (PDF p30).

records.subsection: What monitoring limitations are acknowledged?
records.finding: THE KEY FINDING. The best field measurement in the corpus explicitly does not reach the aquifer where pumping occurs. It measures river-to-alluvium; the link that carries the pumping signal is alluvium-to-180-Foot-Aquifer, and both 2026 studies say independently that they did not measure it.
records.direct_quote: "The study primarily focused on investigating recharge from surface water into the river alluvium and does not examine connectivity to the 180-ft aquifer. Therefore, results do not address (a) the mechanisms for connectivity between the river alluvium and the 180-ft aquifer, and (b) the extent to which additional pumping from the 180-ft aquifer would induce additional recharge from the river." (ISW Report Section 5 Limitations, PDF p32)
records.notes: Record as a METHOD-SCOPE finding, not a criticism: both studies are competent, clearly bounded and transparent about their limits, which is more than much of the corpus. Corroborated independently by the Recharge Evaluation: 'It is unknown whether this water percolates down into the 180-Foot Aquifer and provides local recharge' (PDF p31). | Also touches 1.6 Aquifer Depths — the field study does not reach the aquifer where pumping occurs.

records.subsection: Is the concern of differing depletion at varying aquifer depths recognized?
records.finding: The depth question resolves into a definitional one with real accounting consequences. All pumping is below the Salinas Valley Aquitard; all interconnection is above it. The interconnected zone is excluded from principal-aquifer status because nobody pumps it, and DWR accepted that definition.
records.direct_quote: "The Salinas Valley Aquitard extends across much of the Subbasin and inhibits hydraulic connection between the stream and the underlying principal aquifers where groundwater pumping occurs." (Amendment 1 5.6.2, PDF p191)
records.notes: DWR quoted in Periodic Evaluation 1.1.2 (PDF p21): 'Department staff do not believe the SVBGSA erred in its identification of principal aquifers' and 'the SVBGSA did not act unreasonably when defining principal aquifers.' Stated basis: no extraction from the shallow sediments that is 'significant and economic.' ISW is measured only where the aquitard is absent.

records.subsection: How are you attributing depletion to a specific pump?
records.finding: Not addressed, and - exactly as in Merced - structurally sidestepped without the documents saying so. The paired all-pumping-off simulation avoids superposition error by construction, but no document states this, and the method cannot attribute depletion to any well, field, or GSA. Sharper here than in Merced: the OPERATIVE criterion is a water level at one well, which has no attribution capability at all.

records.subsection: Once a parcel stops pumping, does its paper entitlement to pump get freed up?
records.finding: DESIGN INSIGHT FOR DWR. Acquisition is the only one of the three basins' instruments that is robust to the absence of an allocation system. Merced's and East Turlock's designs both presuppose a functioning entitlement ledger; buying the land removes the pumper rather than regulating them.
records.direct_quote: "The 2020 GSP proposed a Water Charges Framework for the Salinas Valley. Amendment 1 widens the management action to Demand Planning to include other types of demand planning. It separates demand planning from the funding mechanism, so as to not preclude options. Demand planning includes, but is not limited to, pumping allocations, pumping controls, and pumping reductions." (Periodic Evaluation Table 3-1, PDF p91; verified column-aware)
records.notes: STATE THE TRADE-OFF, DO NOT TAKE A SIDE: acquisition is permanent and needs no compliance monitoring, but is capital-intensive, slow (completion 2027, six years after MLRP launch), reaches only willing sellers of marginal land, and - because the GSA does not hold the grant - produces no entry in any SGMA accounting system.

records.subsection: How are those co-benefits tracked and quantified?
records.finding: BEST ECOLOGICAL ACCOUNTING IN THE PROJECT. A per-GDE continuous statistical threshold derived from a regression of vegetation greenness on depth to groundwater, computed only where the relationship is statistically significant, automated in R, and recomputable annually from two public datasets. Merced scores ecological co-benefits by application-stage checkbox; East Turlock uses an optional ordinal visual protocol.
records.direct_quote: "ZDTG threshold = (ZNDVI threshold (i.e. -1) - linear model intercept)/ linear model slope" (GDE report, PDF p19). A GDE is classified of concern for a year if both ZNDVI <= -1 and ZDTG >= ZNDVI.
records.notes: Method follows Rhode et al. (2024), Nature Water. Inputs: Landsat NDVI via TNC GDE Pulse and MCWRA's existing annual groundwater elevations. Only ecological accounting in the project that a platform could run.

records.subsection: How are those co-benefits tracked and quantified?
records.finding: Thresholds are computed only for GDEs showing a statistically significant negative relationship between greenness and depth to groundwater - the method declines to set a threshold where the evidence does not support one.

records.finding: AND THE SEAT IS STRUCTURALLY SUBORDINATED ON THE TWO DECISIONS THAT CONSTITUTE DEMAND MANAGEMENT. records.subsection: How are GSAs / subbasins engaging with the broader community?
records.finding: BEST ANSWER TO THE ENGAGEMENT-METHODOLOGY QUESTION IN THE PROJECT, and it is community-authored. Four named conditions: accessibility, self-efficacy, time commitment/logistics, and relevance. Condition (2) states that participation must make a difference to the outcome - precisely what the Super Majority Plus rule constrains for the DAC, environmental and public directors.
records.direct_quote: "(1) Accessibility - information is accessible, in a language and with sufficient background so that all present can understand what is presented (2) Self-efficacy - community member participation makes a difference in the outcome of this plan and groundwater management (3) Time commitment / logistics - meetings are held in familiar locations, close enough to where community members live or work, and at a time when most are available (4) Relevance - the meeting and information is important enough and relevant for community members to prioritize" (CWC comment letter, 2020 GSP Appendix 11G, PDF p1438) [OCR]
records.notes: THE COMMUNITY'S OWN FRAMEWORK NAMES THE FAILURE MODE THE GOVERNANCE STRUCTURE PRODUCES. Connection available from two verified passages, no speculation required.

records.subsection: Machine-readability of the community record
records.finding: NEW EXTRACTION HAZARD CLASS FOR THE MACHINE-READABILITY THREAD. 31 pages of the 2020 GSP silently drop the letter pair 'ti' from every word containing it - 'informa on' for information, 'cons tuent' for constituent. The affected pages are the Community Water Center's public comment letter, the single richest Community Considerations source in the basin.
records.direct_quote: Signature search across all eight documents found the dropout in the 2020 GSP only, on 31 pages in two contiguous runs: PDF 1408-1410 and 1413-1440. pdffonts reports uni: yes for every font on these pages, so the standard ToUnicode diagnostic PASSES. Pages were rendered at 300 dpi and OCR'd with Tesseract; all quotes from that range are marked [OCR].
records.notes: RECOMMENDED NEW STANDING RULE: screen for systematic character-sequence dropout as well as blank extraction; pdffonts uni: yes does not clear a document. Test with a signature search for common words broken by a missing pair before quoting any appendix. | Outside the current outline: document machine-readability (systematic "ti" character-pair dropout across 31 pages) — cross-cutting format finding with no Community sub-question.

records.subsection: Machine-readability of the comment matrix
records.finding: Appendix 11G is a wide table whose Comment and Response columns interleave under pdftotext -layout. Recovering who said what required rebuilding columns from word bounding boxes and pairing rows by y-coordinate - the same hazard as East Turlock's Attachment C, in a matrix roughly three times the size.
records.direct_quote: Column boundaries 15,150,180,265,512,700 (num, meta, date, commenter, comment, response, docname) are correct for this matrix; at 555 pt the Response column bleeds into Comment and at 465 pt the Comment column truncates mid-sentence. A docname residue still appears at the right edge of the response column.
records.notes: The pairing mattered: the finding that a specific rural well owner's request received the response 'Comment noted.
